# Chapter exercise: ArcGIS Data with arcpullr {.unnumbered}

**Medical Facilities from NC OneMap**

This exercise goes with **Chapter 14, ArcGIS Data with arcpullr**. It builds on the Census Data exercise from Chapter 13, which also downloaded data through an API. It should take you about **one hour**. Read this whole section before you start.

## Purpose

**Skills you'll practice.** By the end of this exercise you will be able to:

1. Read a layer's REST Services Directory page and record its geometry type, coordinate system, record limit, and field names.
2. Download a layer from an ArcGIS feature service into R as an sf object with `get_spatial_layer()`.
3. Write `where` clauses in SQL, with `=`, `IN`, `AND`, and text values in single quotes.
4. Explain why filtering on the server is better than downloading everything and filtering in R.
5. Check, project, map, and save a downloaded layer, and record when you downloaded it.

**Knowledge you'll gain.** You'll find out how many licensed medical facilities North Carolina has, what kinds they are, and how Orange and Durham counties compare.

**Why this matters.** State and local governments publish most of their GIS data (parcels, schools, roads, parks, hospitals) on ArcGIS portals such as NC OneMap. Being able to pull exactly the features you need straight into R, with a script that records where they came from, makes your work faster and reproducible. Portal layers change over time, so knowing how to document a download is part of doing honest analysis.

## Task

Work through Parts 1 to 7 in order, top to bottom. In each part:

- Read the short explanation, then do each step marked with a bullet (•).
- Wherever you see `___`, replace it with the missing code **before** you run the chunk. Where you see `# your code here`, write the code yourself.
- Answer each question (**Q1**, **Q2**, ...) in a sentence or two of Markdown, where it says *Your answer here.*
- This exercise downloads data, so you need an internet connection. The full statewide download in Part 5 takes a little while.
- Your numbers may differ slightly from a classmate's if NC OneMap updates the layer between your downloads. That's expected; say when you downloaded it.

| Part | What you'll do | About |
|:-----|:---------------|:------|
| 1 | Set up your file and load the packages | 4 min |
| 2 | Read the layer's REST page | 10 min |
| 3 | Download one county | 8 min |
| 4 | Write `where` clauses | 12 min |
| 5 | Filter on the server or in R? | 8 min |
| 6 | Project, map, and save | 13 min |
| 7 | Reflect, knit, and turn in | 5 min |

**Turn in** your `.Rmd` file and your knitted `.html` file on Canvas.

## Criteria for success

Use this checklist before you turn your work in. Each item matches a row of the rubric below.

- [ ] The file knits to HTML with no errors, and the author and date at the top are yours.
- [ ] Every `___` and `# your code here` has been filled in, and every chunk runs.
- [ ] Every question (Q1 to Q10) has an answer in complete sentences, using numbers from your output.
- [ ] Every `where` clause uses the field names from the REST page, single quotes around text, and `=` (not `==`).
- [ ] The layer is projected to EPSG:32119 before anything is measured.
- [ ] Your map has a title, a legend title, and credits with your name, "NC OneMap", and the date you downloaded the data.
- [ ] No `install.packages()` line is anywhere in the file.
- [ ] The three reflection questions are answered.

| Criterion | Full credit | Partial credit | No credit |
|:----------|:------------|:---------------|:----------|
| Knits (2 pts) | Knits to HTML with no errors | Knits, but some chunks have errors shown | Doesn't knit, or no HTML turned in |
| REST page (2 pts) | Q1 and Q2 record the details correctly | Some details missing | Not done |
| Downloads and where clauses (5 pts) | Every request correct, with correct SQL | Most correct | Many missing or wrong |
| Questions (7 pts) | Q3 to Q10 answered with numbers and reasons | Some answers missing or without reasons | Most answers missing |
| Map (3 pts) | Projected, with title, legend title, and credits with the download date | Some parts missing | Not done |
| Reflection (1 pt) | All three answered | | Missing |

**What a good answer looks like.** Here is a question, a weak answer, and a strong one.

> *Question:* Why use a `where` clause instead of `filter()`?
>
> *Weak answer:* "It's faster."
>
> *Strong answer:* "With `where`, the server sends only the 61 Orange County facilities instead of all 6,800 in the state, so the download took a fraction of the time. For a big layer like statewide parcels, downloading everything might not even be possible, and the `where` clause also records in my script exactly which features I used."

The strong answer uses numbers from the output, explains *why*, and says when it matters most.

**IMPORTANT!** Save often. Before you knit, choose **Run > Restart R and Run All Chunks** to make sure every chunk works from a fresh start.
